title: Build your own tool, exactly how you want it
summary: The library not quite right? Create your own coping tool from scratch. Mix text prompts, a mood slider, a checklist, and more into a card you actually use inside the app.
body: The curated library is a starting point, not a limit. If the tool you want doesn't exist, you can build it yourself, and it lives right inside the app, not off in another app. Open the menu (the ⋮ at the top right of your wallet) and choose **Create Tool**. Give it a name and an icon, then start adding blocks. Each block is a piece you can use: a **Text Input** or **Text Area** for writing, a **Mood Slider** to rate how you feel, **Choice Buttons** to pick from options, a **Checkbox** for a simple yes, a **Counter** to tally something, even a bit of **Static Text** to remind yourself what to do. Stack them in any order. Say you want a nightly wind-down: add a Mood Slider ("How wound up are you?"), a Text Area ("What's on your mind?"), and a Checkbox ("Screens off"). Save it, and it sits in your wallet like any other card. When you open it, you fill it in right there, and every entry is logged, so it feeds your streaks and Insights just like the built-in tools. This is different from adding an app you launch elsewhere. This tool is yours, and you use it in the moment, inside the app. Start with one block and add from there. Whatever helps you, you can build.

title: Put your go-to tools right on top
summary: Your most-used tools should be the easiest to reach. Rearrange your wallet in seconds so the cards you lean on most are always at the top.
body: Your wallet is personal, so the order of your tools should be too. If the one you reach for every day is buried near the bottom, a few seconds fixes that. Press and hold any card in your wallet. That opens **Reorder Cards**, a simple list of all your tools. Use the up and down arrows next to each one to move it, nudging your favorites toward the top and the ones you rarely touch further down. When it looks right, tap **Done** to save the new order. That's it. The next time you open the app, the tools that matter most are right where you want them, ready the moment you need them.

title: Tidy your wallet without losing anything
summary: Not using a tool right now? Archive it to clear the clutter. It's tucked safely away with all its history, ready to restore whenever you want it back.
body: Your needs change over time, and your wallet can change with them. A tool that helped last month might just be in the way today. Instead of deleting it, you can archive it. Tap the tool to open it, then tap the **⋮** menu and choose **Archive card**. It leaves your wallet right away, so what's left is only what you're actually using now. Nothing is lost: your usage history, streaks, and past entries all stay intact. When you want it back, open the **⋮** menu at the top of your wallet and tap **Archive**. There you'll find everything you've set aside. Tap **Restore to Wallet** on any card and it returns, right where it was. Archiving is always reversible, so there's no pressure. Clear the space you need today, and bring tools back the moment they're useful again.

title: Can't find your app? Add it yourself
summary: If an app you love isn't in the library, make your own card for it in a minute. Give it a name and a link, and launch it from your wallet like any other tool.
body: The library has cards for a lot of popular apps, but it can't cover everything. If the app you rely on isn't there, you don't have to go without. You can add it yourself. Open the menu (the ⋮ at the top right of your wallet) and choose **Create Tool**. Give your card a name and an icon in the first step. In the next step, tap Add block and pick Link Button. That's the piece that turns your card into a launcher. Fill in three things: a Label for the button (like "Open my app"), a Target URL, and an optional Fallback URL. For the target, use the app's website (starting with https://), or its link if you know it. Set the fallback to somewhere useful, like the app's website, so you still land somewhere if the app isn't installed. Then preview and save. Now that card lives in your wallet alongside everything else, and tapping its button opens your app. Your whole toolkit stays in one place, even the parts we didn't think of.

title: Feeling anxious right now? Try this
summary: When anxiety spikes, you don't have to figure out what to do. Open the app, tell it you're anxious, and it points you to tools that fit.
body: When anxiety hits, the last thing you want is to scroll around deciding what might help. So let the app do that part. Open Mental Health Wallet and tap **Start from how I feel**. Choose anxious. It'll suggest tools that tend to help with that state, often a short grounding or breathing exercise you can do right where you are. Pick one and follow it for a minute. Not even sure "anxious" is the word? Use the guided check-in and it'll help you land on what you're feeling first, then suggest from there. You don't have to ride it out alone or white-knuckle through it. A minute with the right tool can take the edge off. Keep this one in your back pocket for the next time it creeps up.

title: Here whenever you need it
summary: No guilt, no streak to protect. If now's a good moment, one 60-second tool is waiting in your wallet.
body: It's been a little while, and that's completely okay. Life gets busy, and a tools app should fit around your life, not nag at it. No streak to keep up, no catching up to do. If right now happens to be a good moment, open your wallet and use one tool. A single 60-second reset counts. If now isn't the time, this email needs nothing from you. Either way, it's here when you need it. That's the point.

title: Welcome to Mental Health Wallet
summary: Glad you're here. Here's what to expect from these emails, and one small thing to try first.

cta.label: Open the app and tap a card

body: Thanks for signing up. Glad to have you. Here's the deal with these emails: every now and then I'll send a short, practical tip to help you get more out of the app, and, if you asked for them, the occasional gentle reminder to come back. No spam, no pressure. You can change what you receive or stop anytime from the link at the bottom of any email. If you want one small thing to try right now: open the app and tap a card to use a tool. That's the whole idea, a small toolkit of things that help, ready when you need them. That's it for now. More soon, and only when it's actually useful.

title: Keep the apps you already use, all in one place
summary: Add apps like Headspace, Calm, and Insight Timer as cards in your wallet and launch them straight from there. Your whole toolkit lives in one place.
body: Mental Health Wallet isn't trying to replace the wellness apps you already like. It's meant to sit on top of everything you use, so your whole toolkit lives in one place. When you go to add tools, you'll find cards for apps like Headspace, Calm, Insight Timer, and more. Add any of them to your wallet, and you can launch the app right from its card. Alongside your quick techniques and your own custom tools, everything sits together, and the app can help point you to the right one based on how you feel. So you don't have to choose between the app you love and having one organized home for your tools. You can have both. Next time you open the app, tap the menu, choose Add Tool, and look for the app cards. Add the one you already use most.

title: Not sure what you need? Start from how you feel
summary: Instead of hunting for the right tool, pick your emotion and let the app suggest what fits. Not sure how you feel? A short guided check-in figures it out with you.

cta.label: Try Start from how I feel

body: Most tools ask you to already know what you're looking for. Mental Health Wallet can work the other way around: start from how you feel, and let it point you to something that fits. On your wallet, tap the **Start from how I feel** card. Pick the emotion that matches where you are right now. The app suggests tools that tend to help with that state, so you spend your energy on the practice, not on searching. Not sure what you're feeling? That happens. Tap the guided check-in instead. It asks a few simple questions about your body, your mind, and your situation, and lands on a feeling with you. From there you get the same tailored suggestions. It takes under a minute, and there's no wrong answer. Next time you open the app and feel a little off but can't name it, this is a good place to start.

title: See which tools actually help you
summary: After you use a tool, the app asks how you feel. Over time it shows you which tools genuinely move the needle for you, so you can lean on what works.

cta.label: Use a tool and check in

body: It's easy to collect coping tools. It's harder to know which ones are actually doing something for you. Mental Health Wallet helps you find out. When you finish using a tool, it asks a simple question: how do you feel now? You pick from calmer, clearer, hopeful, same, or worse. That's it, one tap. Do that a few times and a picture starts to form. The app shows you which tools tend to leave you feeling better, and which ones don't seem to land for you. Instead of guessing, you get to lean on the tools that genuinely help, and quietly retire the ones that don't. Next time you use a tool, take the extra second to answer the check-in. Future you will have real data to work with.

title: Track the thing that matters to you
summary: You choose what getting better means to you during setup, then the daily check-in tracks how you're doing against your own measure, not a generic score.
body: "Getting better" means different things to different people. For one person it's managing stress; for another it's sleeping better, or feeling more present. Mental Health Wallet lets you define it on your own terms. During setup you pick what success means to you. From then on, the daily check-in, the seedling button on your wallet, lets you log how you're tracking against that personal measure. Not a one-size-fits-all wellness score, but the thing you actually care about. Over time those check-ins become a simple, honest record of your own progress. Some days up, some days down, and that's fine. The point is to see the trend in your own words. If you set a personal measure during setup, try tapping the seedling today and logging where you're at. It only takes a moment.

title: Why does this tool work? Tap Learn more
summary: Every tool in the library has a Learn more link that explains how it works, the evidence behind it, and where to read further. No blind trust required.

cta.label: Open a tool and tap Learn more

body: A coping tool is easier to use when you understand why it's supposed to help. So the tools that come with Mental Health Wallet don't just tell you what to do, they show you the reasoning. Open any library tool and look for the **Learn more** link in its description. Tap it and you'll see a plain-language explanation: how the technique works, the level of evidence behind it, and a short summary of what research shows. For the ones where it makes sense, there are further reading links so you can go deeper. It's expert-sourced, not marketing. The idea is simple: you should be able to answer "why should I trust this?" before you rely on it. Next time a tool catches your eye, tap Learn more before you use it. A little context makes the practice land better.
